messages:
lucy-sales: New lead (Northgate) needs an LLM POC where PCI/PHI flows go via their on‑prem DLP, non-sensitive traffic goes to Redwood hosted. They want options + rough cost/ops notes by EOD.

omar-solutions: Options quick list: 1) VPC peering/TGW -> route sensitive subnets to customer egress (preserves src IP if configured). 2) Interface PrivateLink to our connector -> customer proxy pulls from our endpoint (simpler, but usually NATs client IP). 3) Route-based split at app layer (model routing): tag sensitive models -> send to private deployment.

tess-netops: NetOps constraints they stated: no wide 0.0.0.0/0 allowlists; need SNI visible for their TLS-inspectors; prefer original client IP in logs for audit.

ben-security: For POC recommend TLS passthrough to avoid cert mgmt and big compliance hit. If MITM required, customer must provide certs and written handling for secrets/PII.

omar-solutions: Minimal firewall snippet to hand to them: `allow 203.0.113.0/24 tcp/443 to redwood-edge; allow DNS to their resolver only; allow SNI *.redwood.ai` — we'll replace with real CIDRs in handoff.

deploy-bot: perf-estimate: proxying adds ~15-60ms depending on geolocation; if >150 concurrent streams recommend temporary Dedicated burst.

lucy-sales: Pricing/answers needed: who pays PrivateLink infra? And will proxying change Redwood pricing?

omar-solutions: AWS charges for interface endpoints go to customer. Redwood: no per-request surcharge but Dedicated capacity or burst nodes may be needed for sustained proxied throughput (billable). I'll attach a short estimate.

tess-netops: If they insist on src-IP preservation, they must deploy an NLB with proxy-protocol v2 in front of our connector and we must enable proxy-protocol on our side. That requires ops changes both sides.

ben-security: CISO blurb: "Routing regulated inference through customer-controlled network devices keeps DLP and inspection inside your boundary. Customer is responsible for cert management, proxy config, firewall allowlists, and audit retention of client identifiers. Redwood supplies the private endpoint and validates connectivity; any on-path TLS interception must be approved by both security teams."

lucy-sales: Action items: @omar-solutions prepare Dedicated/burst estimate, @tess-netops prepare exact allowlist snippet with final CIDRs, @ben-security finalize the CISO paragraph. I'll send to Northgate tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
